title: Going Live in Malaysia
subtitle: Opening balances, cut-over, SST and MyInvois — plus a 90-day path to mastery
outcomes: Run a go-live with a rollback plan instead of hope
Load opening balances that tie to the audited numbers
Configure a Malaysian site end to end, including e-Invoicing
Operate, monitor and keep learning after the consultant leaves

slides.title: The go-live gate
bullets: Masters complete: items, parties, prices, taxes, warehouses, cost centres — reviewed by the people who will use them
UAT signed off on the ten transactions that matter most, run by real users with real data volumes
Opening balances prepared in a spreadsheet that already ties to the audited trial balance
Training delivered per role, a named super-user per department, and a help channel that is not one exhausted consultant
slides.notes: A go-live fails for organisational reasons far more often than technical ones. The gate is not 'the software is ready'; it is 'the business can run on it on Monday'. If a department cannot name a super-user who has already completed their own transactions, that department is not ready, whatever the checklist says.

callout.title: No rollback, no go-live
callout.text: Agree in writing what triggers a rollback and who may call it. Deciding that at 2am on Sunday is how projects die.

slides.title: Opening balances that survive an audit
bullets: Stock: Stock Reconciliation or an opening Material Receipt per warehouse, valued at the agreed cost
Receivables and payables: opening Sales and Purchase Invoices, not journals, so ageing and reconciliation work
Bank and equity: an opening Journal Entry for everything else, balanced against an 'Opening Balance Equity' account
Reconcile the result to the audited trial balance before the first real transaction, and lock the numbers in a signed document
slides.notes: The temptation is to jam everything into one opening journal because it balances. Resist: invoices are what make dunning, ageing and payment reconciliation possible, and stock documents are what make valuation possible. The opening balance is a one-time chance to start clean, and the cost of doing it properly is a few days.

rows: Valuation and quantities must enter the stock ledger
Ageing, dunning and allocation need invoices
Register must agree to the GL

slides.title: The weekend runbook
bullets: Freeze: stop invoicing and stock movements in the old system at an agreed timestamp, and tell customers
Load in order: company and accounts → masters → opening stock → opening AR/AP → bank and equity journals
Verify: trial balance, stock balance, AR/AP ageing and a test invoice all match the agreed numbers
Switch, then hypercare: daily stand-up for two weeks, one queue for issues, one person deciding what is a bug
slides.notes: Write the runbook as a numbered list with timestamps, owners and a verification step after each block. Rehearse it on a staging copy, timed. The rehearsal is what turns a terrifying weekend into a checklist, and it usually reveals that the master data export is the long pole, not the software.

callout.title: Run it twice
callout.text: A full dry run on staging, then delete the site and do it again. The second run is the one that goes smoothly in production.

slides.title: Backups, staging and upgrades
bullets: Automated daily backups, checked weekly by restoring into a scratch site — an untested backup is a rumour
Keep a staging site with production-like data for testing upgrades, patches and customisations
Pin Frappe and ERPNext versions; upgrade on a schedule with a rollback plan and a changelog review
Test custom apps and print formats after every upgrade — that is where breakage hides
slides.notes: The restore drill is non-negotiable. Do it quarterly, on a machine someone else can reach, and time it. You are not testing whether backups exist; you are testing whether the business can be back in an hour. The same discipline applies to upgrades: patch notes, staging, verification, and a documented way back.

slides.title: Hardening a site that holds the company's money
bullets: Two-factor authentication for every user who can pay, cancel or approve; a separate integration user for APIs
Least privilege: no shared logins, no System Manager for daily work, role profiles reviewed quarterly
Protect secrets: API keys per integration, rotate on staff departure, keep client secrets in Password fields only
Restrict network exposure — VPN or IP allowlist for admin, HTTPS everywhere, and an audit of who can export data
slides.notes: Most ERPNext breaches are not clever: they are a shared admin password, an API key in a spreadsheet, or a former employee with a live login. Review the user list monthly, disable rather than delete, and treat data export rights as sensitive. Frappe gives you the tools; discipline is the rest.

callout.title: Leavers checklist
callout.text: Disable the user, revoke API keys, rotate shared secrets, remove from role profiles. Put it in the HR offboarding form, not in someone's memory.

slides.title: Configuring the Malaysian site
bullets: SST: sales and service tax templates with separate liability accounts, tax categories per supply type, and a monthly SST-02 reconciliation
e-Invoice: install erpnext_malaysia, set the MyInvois client credentials, company TIN/BRN/SST, customer TINs and MSIC codes, then test in Sandbox
Operate LHDN rules: submit on invoice day, 72-hour cancellation window with a reason, credit notes referencing the original UUID, TIN validation before billing a new customer
Stock on the floor: the mobile_inventory PWA posts receipts, issues, transfers and counts offline and syncs when the signal returns
slides.notes: This is the chapter where the course becomes local. Test the whole chain in the MyInvois sandbox before the first real invoice: TIN validation, submission, validation polling, and a cancellation. Then agree two written policies the day you go live — who may cancel an e-Invoice, and what happens when a buyer rejects one. Both will be needed within the first month.

slides.title: The weekly health check
bullets: Scheduler running, Error Log reviewed, background queue drained, backups restored last week
Unallocated payments, unreconciled bank lines, negative stock and open work orders trending to zero
Pipeline of failed e-Invoice submissions empty, with every error either fixed or documented
One dashboard per role, reviewed in a standing fifteen-minute meeting
slides.notes: Systems do not fail suddenly; they decay. A fifteen-minute weekly review of five numbers prevents the quarterly crisis. Assign each number an owner and make the meeting about the exception, not the report. If a metric has been red for three weeks, either fix it or stop measuring it — a permanently red metric teaches people to ignore the dashboard.

slides.title: Your next ninety days
bullets: Days 1–30: rebuild this course's labs on a throwaway site; break things deliberately and fix them
Days 31–60: own one real business process end to end — selling or buying — including its month-end reconciliation
Days 61–90: write something reusable: a print format, a report, an app, or a runbook your successor could follow
Read the source when documentation runs out: the DocType JSON and the controller tell the truth about behaviour
slides.notes: Mastery is not knowing every feature; it is predicting what a change will do to the ledgers. The fastest route is deliberate practice on a site you are allowed to destroy, followed by ownership of a process whose numbers you have to defend. After that, contributing — a patch, a report, a documented gotcha — is how the knowledge sticks.

callout.title: The one habit that compounds
callout.text: Keep a running notes file of every surprise: what you expected, what happened, what the fix was. In a year it is worth more than any course.

lab.title: Capstone: take a company live in a day
steps: Provision a fresh site; create the company, chart of accounts, cost centres and warehouses from a written plan
Import items, customers, suppliers, price lists and tax templates; prove them with two draft transactions
Load opening stock, three opening customer invoices, two supplier invoices and a bank journal that balances to a trial balance
Run the full sales cycle for one of those customers, including a partial delivery and a payment; run the full purchase cycle including a receipt and a payment
Manufacture one product from a BOM and reconcile its valuation to the components consumed
Configure Malaysia E-Invoice Settings in Sandbox, validate a TIN, submit one invoice, poll its status, then cancel it with a reason
Close the month: bank reconciliation, accrual journal with reversal, depreciation, period closing voucher, and export the submission log
Write a two-page handover: the runbook, the rollback triggers and the weekly health check, in your own words
lab.done: A stranger can read your handover, restart the site from backup, and run a compliant invoice without asking you anything.

quiz.question: Why should opening receivables be invoices rather than a journal entry?
options: Journals are not allowed after go-live
Ageing, allocation and dunning work per invoice; a journal leaves an unallocated lump sum
quiz.why: The Payment Ledger settles per invoice. A journal balances the account but produces nothing to allocate or chase.

quiz.question: What makes a backup trustworthy?
options: It has been restored into a working site within a measured time
quiz.why: Only a completed restore proves recoverability; everything else is an assumption about files you have not opened.

quiz.question: A buyer rejects an e-Invoice in MyInvois. What is the supplier's next step?
options: Cancel the document at LHDN within the allowed window and issue a corrected invoice
quiz.why: A rejection request only asks for cancellation; the supplier must cancel and re-issue. Editing a submitted invoice is never the answer.

quiz.question: Which go-live signal matters most?
options: Real users completing their own transactions in UAT with a named super-user per department
Consultants on site for a week
quiz.why: Adoption is the risk. Completed transactions by real users, with local support, predict survival far better than configuration completeness.

quiz.question: What is the fastest route to ERPNext mastery?
options: Deliberate practice on a disposable site, then owning a process whose numbers you must defend
quiz.why: You learn the system by predicting its effect on the ledgers and being corrected. Ownership of real numbers forces that feedback loop.

narration: Chapter ten takes the course live. Make the gate organisational rather than technical: masters reviewed by the people who use them, UAT signed off on the ten transactions that matter, opening balances tying to the audited trial balance, and a named super-user in every department. If nobody can name that person, the department is not ready. Agree in writing what triggers a rollback and who can call it. Opening balances are a one-time chance to start clean. Load stock through stock documents so valuation enters the ledger. Load receivables and payables as opening invoices, not journals, so ageing, allocation and dunning work. Put everything else in an opening journal against opening balance equity, and reconcile before the first real transaction. Write the cut-over as a timed runbook with a verification step after each block, and rehearse it on staging twice. Afterwards: test a restore quarterly, keep a staging site, pin versions, and review custom apps after every upgrade. Harden security with two-factor authentication, least privilege and a leavers checklist. Then the Malaysian specifics: separate SST liability accounts, a monthly reconciliation, and the e-invoice app tested end to end in sandbox, including a cancellation with a reason, before your first real invoice. Agree two policies on day one: who may cancel an e-invoice, and what happens when a buyer rejects one. Mastery is predicting what a change does to the ledgers.
